text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Polish Airlines LOT will introduce lower weekend fares on European connections for the winter holiday season as of January 10, LOT said.

- Over 15,000 firms from 58 countries exhibited their products at 27 international trade exhibitions organised by the Poznan-based Miedzynarodowe Targi Poznanskie international fair organiser, the new MTP president Boguslaw Zalewski said.
- The stock of the privatised TPSA telecom monopolist could be issued on the Polish and international stock exchanges in mid-1998, the telecommunications ministry said.

- Poland's importers paid almost 28 billion zlotys in customs duties in 1996, which exceeded the finance ministry's forecast by 11.7 percent and was 27.5 percent higher than the year before, the finance ministry said.

- The PKO SA brokerage house will produce a share issue prospectus for the Krakow-based Wawel SA confectionary maker, Wawel's president Wladyslaw Kaczmarczyk said. Wawel holds a seven percent market share and plans to increase it further.

- The Bauma SA construction firm, to issue shares soon, said it has high profit margins but its liquidity ratio is unsatifactory and the share issue should improve it. The company will apply for a listing on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market, Bauma said.

- In spite of previous announcements Thailand has not introduced anti-dumping customs duties on wide flange beam imports from Poland sold there by the listed Stalexport and the Huta Katowice steel plant.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Polish Business Club (PKB) named Ryszard Pienkowski, owner of the Infor publishing firm, and the listed Budimex's president Grzegorz Tuderek as businessmen of the year.

- Poland's deep sea fishing trawlers have stopped pollock fishing in the Bering and Okhotsk sea area as Poland and Russia are negotiating the allowed pollock fishing quotas. Polish trawlers are losing $25,000 daily through the forced breaks, the Swinoujscie-based Odra deep sea fishing firm said.

- The Warsaw-based Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environment protection bank and the Poligrafia SA printing firm, controlled by the Exbud capital group, have applied for a share listing on the Warsaw bourse's main market, they said.
- The listed BICK construction firm will carry out construction works for the Radom-based ZPT cigarette maker worth 1.2 million zlotys, BICK said.
- The listed DomPlast plastic maker will invest seven million zlotys in new machinery, the company said.
- The listed PLI wholesale and retail firm plans to issue commercial paper of 50 million zlotys nominal value.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Poznan-based MTP international fair organiser's annual net profit in 1996 should reach 30 million zlotys, the MTP deputy president Przemyslaw Trawa said.
- Poland's value added tax (VAT) system is much more complicated and burdensome than the equivalent EU regulations, the EU Commercial Chambers' Forum said.
- The Pekao SA banking group has contracted Arthur Anderson to produce the group's operational strategy, Pekao group board member and the PBG bank president Andrzej Szukalski said.
ZYCIE
- France's Renault automaker sold 20,616 cars in Poland last year, which showed a 130 percent growth compared with the year before.
- Petrobank will be the motor of the LG Group's investment in central and eastern Europe, LG Group board member Dong Chang Park said.
PARKIET
- The U.S.-based Carnegie Bank has recommended buying the shares of the Magna Polonia National Investment Fund (NFI) in a development strategy report produced recently.

- The listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) bank's net profit was 55.2 million zlotys in the accounting year 1995/1996, which showed a 5.4 million zlotys decline compared with the year before, BIG said.
